subject: Next steps: price scouting & target $/1M for BrightLeaf integration
messages:
From: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.ai>
To: Jared Liu <jared@brightleaf.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 22 May 2026 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Next steps: price scouting & target $/1M for BrightLeaf integration

Hi Jared — great call earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned on target economics before I run a formal pilot proposal:  

Recap from discovery:
- Workload: user-facing summary generation + semantic search enrichment for internal analytics.
- Expected steady-state: ~100–300M tokens/month (peaks during product releases).
- Typical input/output sequence lengths: median 220 tokens / request, 95th pct 1.2k (attached sample CSV).

Commercial info you shared:
- BrightLeaf preferred budget band: roughly $10k–$40k / month initially (flex by quarter).
- Procurement requires a clear $/1M tokens anchor for TCO comparison vs internal hosts.

Initial Redwood benchmarking (informal):
- OpenAI: approx $20–25 per 1M tokens (varies by model & context window).
- Anthropic: approx $18–22 per 1M tokens for comparable completion workloads.
- Common open-model hosts (self-hosted / managed): wide range $8–$30 per 1M tokens depending on ops assumptions (quantization, batching, cache hit-rate).

Where we need your input to refine a target price:
1) Confirm committed monthly volume range: is 100–300M accurate for Q3 baseline?
2) Does the budget band above reflect gross spend or net after discounts/credits?
3) Any hard SLA or data residency constraints beyond US-only?

Proposed immediate next steps:
- You: confirm 1–3 above by EOD Tuesday.
- Us (Redwood): run a short price-sensitivity matrix and three-target scenarios ($/1M): conservative ($22), mid ($14), aggressive ($9) and return a 1-page comparison against OpenAI/Anthropic + a recommended pilot configuration.
- If the mid or aggressive targets look feasible, we’ll draft a 3-month pilot term sheet and an expected TTM cost model.

Attachments: brightleaf_mau_and_seq_lengths.csv, redwood_price_grid_v1.pdf (informal grid).

Thanks — feel free to call if you want to walk through the numbers live.

—Logan
Logan Wright
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
Calendly: https://calendly.com/logan-redwood/30
From: Jared Liu <jared@brightleaf.ai>
To: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 22 May 2026 16:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Next steps: price scouting & target $/1M for BrightLeaf integration

Thanks Logan — appreciate the clear recap. Quick answers inline and a couple clarifications:  

1) Committed volume: yes, 100–300M is our best estimate for Q3. We can commit to a minimum of 100M/mo as part of an initial pilot, with the expectation of hitting ~250M by month 3 if latency and cost look good.

2) Budget band: $10k–$40k is what our product org has available to start. That is gross spend — procurement will request discounts for committed volumes.

3) SLA/residency: US-only for now; we do require access logs and audit traces for the integration (SOC2 is a plus).

On pricing targets: product leadership is looking for a ~ $10–15 per 1M token target to make this unit-econ positive for our use case. If Redwood can show reasonable latency and a clear plan to get to ~$12/1M at scale (100–300M) we can push procurement to prioritize.

Next steps from our side:
- I’ll get procurement contact and include them if we move to term discussion (should be by early next week).
- Attached: procurement baseline email (sent separately) and a short note on expected batch sizes (will follow).

Jared
Jared Liu
Head of Platform | BrightLeaf AI
jared@brightleaf.ai
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 22 May 2026 18:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Next steps: price scouting & target $/1M for BrightLeaf integration

Looping in Vanessa for SE/finance alignment. Quick thoughts:  

- Target anchoring: Jared’s $10–15/1M is aggressive but plausible if we optimize caching and use a quantized variant for embeddings and cheaper completion paths for short replies. We should model three variants with assumed cache hit rates: 10%, 30%, 50%.
- Latency constraint: BrightLeaf mentioned user-facing summaries; we should propose a 95th latency SLO (under 600ms for median workflows) for the pilot, and a fallback to a cheaper model when load spikes.

Action items I can own:
1) Build a 3-scenario TCO spreadsheet (attached as proposed_pilot_term_sheet.pdf) with line items: tokens, infra overhead, ops, discounts.
2) Draft a short pilot term sheet (3 months, 100M committed, escalator to 250M) with option to renew.

Vanessa — can you run a quick check on whether we can feasibly recommend a $12/1M mid target for a committed 250M/mo case (with typical Redwood EC2/GPU mixes)? If yes, we’ll present the mid-scenario as our recommended anchor.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
From: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.ai>
To: Jared Liu <jared@brightleaf.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>, procurement@brightleaf.ai
Date: Sat, 23 May 2026 09:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Next steps: price scouting & target $/1M for BrightLeaf integration

Thanks all — short alignment and proposed timeline:  

- Jared: we’ll treat $10–15/1M as the product team target. Ben/Vanessa will run the 3-scenario TCO with cache-hit assumptions and recommend one anchor. Expect the spreadsheet + recommended anchor by Tue, May 26 EOD.
- If the anchor is $12/1M at 250M committed, we’ll prepare a 3-month pilot term sheet and a DocuSign link for legal/procurement review.
- I’ll book a 30-min follow-up for Wed (26th) to walk the numbers live — calendar invite: https://calendly.com/logan-redwood/30 (please accept).

Deliverables:
1) Redwood: 3-scenario cost model + recommended anchor (Tue EOD) — Ben
2) BrightLeaf: procurement contact + confirmation of gross budget band (Tue EOD) — Jared
3) Redwood: draft pilot term sheet & preliminary DocuSign (if anchor accepted) — Vanessa/Ben

Thanks — looking forward.

—Logan
Logan Wright
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
Attachments: brightleaf_mau_and_seq_lengths.csv, redwood_price_grid_v1.pdf, proposed_pilot_term_sheet.pdf
